parsed.explanation: No criminalisation of trans expression is documented: same-sex conduct is lawful (2012 strike-down, confirmed in the Oct 2024 UPR submission), and there is no presentation or cross-dressing offence. Institutional signals are genuinely positive — the only LGBTI organisation operates freely in all ten districts with a good working relationship with police, which intervened to protect a lesbian in Dec 2015, and Pride has been police-escorted annually since 2013. Against that: no general anti-discrimination protection; a 2017 legal analysis flags that a trans traveller whose passport marker mismatches presentation could face a charge (open question, no documented enforcement); the Oct 2024 submission records discrimination, rape and assaults against LGBT people and health/education barriers but gives no dates or trans-specific detail; the 2016 report notes stigma, taboo and under-reporting. Absence of legal gender recognition and of facility/custody/screening/care evidence is a resident gap or open question, not a documented exposure. Net: above the widespread-discrimination tier, below jurisdictions documenting visitor-facing acceptance or working remedies.
